newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mulls re-export of imported rice as food aid.
newsitem.headline: Japan mulls re-export of imported rice as food aid.

text.p: Japan is considering re-exporting as food aid rice it is obliged to import under a world trade pact, Agriculture Minister Ichizo Ohara said on Tuesday.
The idea is being considered as a way to reduce excessive domestic stocks of the crop, Ohara told reporters.
"The thing is, we're now buying unnecessary rice. Should we dump the imported rice in the sea?" he said. "There's nothing wrong with re-exporting foreign rice to poor countries."
He said the Agriculture and Foreign Ministries would start technical discussions on the idea.

The Agriculture Ministry has estimated that domestic rice stocks at the end of October -- the end of the crop year -- stood at three million tonnes, almost double the 1.61 million tonnes of a year ago.
Good harvests in the past two years have swollen stocks in grain warehouses across the country. A stock level of 1.5 million tonnes is considered desirable throughout the year.

Under the 1993 Uruguay Round world trade agreement, Japan agreed to gradually open its rice market and committed itself to importing 511,000 tonnes of rice during this fiscal year to the end of next March.
It has bought only 155,300 tonnes so far this fiscal year.
